issues.title: fix(physics): Case 600 series peak_heating under-prediction (610, 630, 640)
issues.body:
## Problem Statement

Cases 610, 630, and 640 show systematic peak_heating under-prediction while simultaneously showing peak_cooling over-prediction. This bidirectional error is the signature of a discrete-node solar-injection pathology documented in KNOWN_ISSUES.md LIMIT-05.

| Case | Metric | Fluxion | Reference Band | Deviation |
|------|--------|---------|----------------|----------|
| 610 | peak_heating | 3.26 kW | 4.30–5.70 kW | −24.2% UNDER |
| 630 | peak_heating | 3.16 kW | 4.70–6.10 kW | −32.8% UNDER |
| 640 | peak_heating | 3.13 kW | 4.30–5.70 kW | −27.2% UNDER |

**Source**: `docs/ASHRAE140_RESULTS.md` (2026-07-31 snapshot)

## Evidence
- Test: `cargo test --test ashrae_140_case_600_series`
- KNOWN_ISSUES.md §LIMIT-05 UPDATE (post-#1457 revisit) documents the 14 remaining failures
- `tests/known_issues_regression.rs::issue_1457_case_600_series_tracking` reproduces all 14 metrics

## Impact

These failures block improvement of the ASHRAE 140 pass rate from the current 18.8%. The 5R1C model architectural limitation is documented but the exact mathematical root cause in the solar-injection / timestep integration needs further investigation.

## Root Cause Hypothesis

Per LIMIT-05 UPDATE, the simultaneous peak_heating UNDER + peak_cooling OVER pattern cannot be fixed by adjusting thermal mass constants — it requires either:
1. Sub-hour air-node sub-stepping (reduces dt/τ from ~3.6 to manageable values)
2. GaugeSolver rework (#1465) treating solar as geometric curvature rather than per-timestep energy injection

## Suggested Approach

1. **Immediate**: Verify that `solar_distribution_to_air = 0.7` is being applied correctly in the 5R1C path for the Case 600 series geometry
2. **Short-term**: Investigate whether the 1-hour timestep with dt/τ ≈ 3.6 causes discrete-node oscillation in the air-node temperature
3. **Long-term**: Phase 1b GaugeSolver production wiring (#1462) as architecturally correct fix

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Cases 610, 630, 640 peak_heating within ±15% of reference band midpoints
- [ ] No regression in Cases 600, 620, 650 metrics

issues.title: fix(physics): SOLAR-04 night ventilation broken — Case 650 under-predicts, Case 950 over-predicts by 100x
issues.body:
## Problem Statement

Night ventilation cases show bidirectional failure: Case 650 (low-mass) under-predicts cooling while Case 950 (high-mass) massively over-predicts. Both cases should show significant cooling reduction from night ventilation.

| Case | Metric | Fluxion | Reference | Deviation |
|------|--------|---------|-----------|-----------|
| 650 | annual_cooling | 4430 kWh | 4820–7060 kWh | −10% UNDER |
| 950 | annual_cooling | 105,439 kWh | 390–920 kWh | **+11,400% OVER** |
| 950 | peak_cooling | 68.60 kW | 0.70–0.90 kW | **+7,600% OVER** |

**Source**: `docs/ASHRAE140_RESULTS.md:31-47`

## Evidence

- Test: `tests/known_issues_regression.rs::test_solar04_night_ventilation_regression` — `#[ignore]` quarantine
- KNOWN_ISSUES.md §SOLAR-04: Night ventilation parameter exists but may not be correctly applied
- `physics_impl.rs` lines 927, 3300: `ventilation_airflow` hardcoded to `10000.0 m³/s` (placeholder TODO)

## Impact

- Night ventilation is a core ASHRAE 140 passive cooling strategy — if it doesn't work, the model cannot be used for passive cooling design
- Case 950 result (105 MWh) is physically impossible — more cooling energy than entire building heat gain could account for
- Blocks the `ASHRAE 140 Strict Energy Gate (Issue #1333)`

## Root Cause Hypothesis

1. `ventilation_airflow` is hardcoded to `10000.0 m³/s` instead of reading from building specification (physics_impl.rs TODO)
2. Night ventilation rate may not be multiplied during night hours (22:00–07:00) as specified in ASHRAE 140
3. Case 950 may have double-counting in the air-node energy balance causing exponential accumulation

## Suggested Approach

1. **Fix ventilation_airflow TODO**: Replace hardcoded `10000.0` with actual value from building spec
2. **Trace night ventilation flow**: Verify `NightVentilation` struct in `fluxion-core/src/ashrae_cases.rs` is read correctly
3. **Verify ACH multiplication**: Check if ventilation rate is multiplied in night hours in `step_physics`
4. **Add energy breakdown test**: Trace per-hour Q_cooling, Q_night_vent, Q_mass for Case 950

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Case 650 annual cooling within ±15% of reference midpoints
- [ ] Case 950 annual cooling within ±15% of reference band (390–920 kWh)
- [ ] Case 950 peak_cooling within ±15% of reference band (0.70–0.90 kW)
- [ ] Night ventilation test shows measurable cooling reduction vs non-ventilated baseline

issues.title: fix(physics): SOLAR-03 shading sensitivity — Cases 610/630/910/930 show minimal cooling reduction
issues.body:
## Problem Statement

Cases 610, 630 (low-mass) and 910, 930 (high-mass) test shading devices. Reference programs show **30-60% cooling reduction** with shading. Fluxion shows **minimal or no effect**.

| Case | Fluxion | vs Baseline | Expected Reduction |
|------|---------|-------------|-------------------|
| 610 (south shade) | 4435 kWh | −17% | 30-60% |
| 630 (E/W shade) | 2361 kWh | −56% | 30-60% |
| 910 (south shade) | 7969 kWh | +7.5% | 30-60% |
| 930 (E/W shade) | 5618 kWh | −24% | 40-60% |

**Source**: `docs/ASHRAE140_RESULTS.md:31-46`

## Evidence

- KNOWN_ISSUES.md §SOLAR-03: "shading coefficient not propagating correctly through thermal network"
- `src/sim/shading.rs`: `shaded_fraction` calculated but may not be applied to correct flux term

## Impact

- Shading is a fundamental passive cooling strategy — if it doesn't work, the model cannot be used for building design optimization
- 4 of 6 shading-variant cases fail, dragging overall pass rate below 60% threshold

## Root Cause Hypothesis

1. `shaded_fraction` may be calculated correctly but not applied to the `phi_sol` term in zone heat balance
2. Shading device geometry (overhang depth, fin dimensions) may be incorrectly interpreted
3. Night ventilation interaction may be interfering with shading calculations

## Suggested Approach

1. **Isolate shading contribution**: Add test that traces shading reduction independently of other case differences
2. **Verify flux application**: Check that `phi_sol` reduction from shading is applied in `thermal_model_physics::compute_solar_gain`
3. **Compare geometries**: Verify `ShadingDevice` struct dimensions match ASHRAE 140 Table 1-12N specifications

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Case 610 annual cooling reduction ≥30% vs Case 600 baseline
- [ ] Case 910 annual cooling reduction ≥30% vs Case 900 baseline
- [ ] Shading isolation test passes with documented tolerance

issues.title: fix(physics): Roof-solar gain under-counted ~3x — blocks Case 900+ peak cooling closure
issues.body:
## Problem Statement

Horizontal-surface (roof) solar irradiance is under-counted by approximately 3× in the 9R4C multi-node thermal model, causing Case 900 series peak cooling to be dramatically under-predicted.

| Case | Fluxion Peak Cooling | ASHRAE 140 Ref | Deviation |
|------|---------------------|----------------|-----------|
| 900  | 0.86 kW            | 2.10–3.50 kW  | **−69% UNDER** |
| 950  | 0.84 kW            | 5.30–6.80 kW  | **−86% UNDER** |
| 960  | 0.85 kW            | 6.00–7.50 kW  | **−87% UNDER** |

**Source**: `docs/investigations/issue-1280-ctf-peak-load.md §4`

## Evidence

- `src/sim/thermal_model_physics.rs:2602-2606`: `gains_roof = opaque_solar_w * 0.4` — 60/40 wall/roof split is a hardcoded heuristic
- `KNOWN_ISSUES.md:601`: "roof-solar under-counting (~3×) — routed to GaugeSolver"

## Impact

- LIMIT-05: 14 remaining Case 600-series metrics remain out-of-band
- Blocks the `ASHRAE 140 Strict Energy Gate (Issue #1333)`
- SOLAR-02: High-mass annual cooling under-predicted 30–80%

## Root Cause Hypothesis

The roof solar gain routing to the 9R4C mass nodes uses a fixed 40% fraction instead of deriving from surface-area geometry. For Case 900 with a flat roof, the actual fraction should be `A_roof / (A_wall + A_roof + A_floor)` weighted by incident irradiance.

## Suggested Approach

1. **Compute geometry-based distribution**: Replace `gains_roof = opaque_solar_w * 0.4` with area-weighted fraction
2. **Trace roof irradiance**: Verify `solar_gain_distribution.rs` computes per-surface irradiance correctly
3. **Cross-validate**: Compare against EnergyPlus hourly roof solar values for Denver TMY3

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Case 900 peak_cooling within ±15% of reference band (2.10–3.50 kW)
- [ ] Case 950 peak_cooling within ±15% of reference band (5.30–6.80 kW)
- [ ] Annual energy within ±15% for Cases 900-960

issues.title: fix(gauge-solver): GaugeSolver Phase 1b — Production wiring incomplete
issues.body:
## Problem Statement

The `GaugeSolver` and `MultiZoneGaugeSolver` exist as shadow-mode solvers but are NOT wired into the primary thermal model path. The zone-level heat balance still uses the legacy 5R1C/9R4C lumped-capacitance networks.

**Evidence**:
- `src/physics/gauge_zone_solver.rs:1-5`: Module doc states "replacing the lumped 5R1C zone network with a geometrically-accurate assembly of 1D per-surface GaugeSolvers" — but not yet shipped
- `src/thermal/physics_adapter.rs:94-122`: `gauge_solver` is consulted after the primary solve and stored in `gauge_flux_result` — purely diagnostic
- `ARCHITECTURE.md Module 6`: Phase 1b (#1462) "replaces the stub with the full Christoffel-symbol transport" — not yet shipped

## Impact

- The 14 remaining Case 600-series metrics that require GaugeSolver cannot close
- `test_issue1457_remaining_600_series_metrics` remains `#[ignore]`-quarantined
- Release gate `ASHRAE 140 Strict Energy Gate (Issue #1333)` remains blocked

## Root Cause

`ThermalModelTrait::solve_timesteps` calls `step_physics()` which uses the legacy thermal network. The `GaugeSolver` path is gated behind `PhysicsAdapter::gauge_solver` which is never set as the primary solver.

## Suggested Approach

1. Add solver-selection flag to `ThermalModelTrait` to choose between legacy and GaugeSolver
2. Wire `GaugeSolver` as the primary zone solver when enabled
3. Verify 5R1C fallback still works for non-GaugeSolver configurations

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] GaugeSolver can be selected as primary solver via feature flag
- [ ] Cases 600-640 metrics improve when GaugeSolver is enabled
- [ ] No regression in cases that don't use GaugeSolver
- [ ] `test_issue1457_remaining_600_series_metrics` passes

issues.title: fix(gauge-solver): Phase 3 GaugeSolver Case 900 annual energy — synthetic CSV vs real E+ data
issues.body:
## Problem Statement

GaugeSolver Phase 3 validation harness (`tests/gauge_validation_case_900.rs`) uses a **synthetic analytical CSV** rather than real EnergyPlus hourly data. The current CSV is computed from the documented GaugeSolver formula, not from EnergyPlus.

**Evidence**:

The GaugeSolver Phase 3 validation cannot confirm that the gauge-theoretic approach matches EnergyPlus on annual energy basis. This is the key validation milestone for the gauge-theory research program (#1461, #1462, #1464).

## Suggested Approach

1. **Generate EnergyPlus hourly reference**: Run `tests/reference_data/energyplus_models/ashrae_140_case_900.idf` with EnergyPlus 25.2.0 + Denver TMY3
2. **Replace synthetic CSV**: Update `case_900_diurnal_reference.csv` with E+ hourly data
3. **Enable ignored tests**: Remove `#[ignore]` from `test_case_900_annual_energy_within_15_percent`

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Diurnal swing and phase lag validated against real E+ data

issues.title: fix(physics): Fix ventilation_airflow TODO in physics_impl.rs — hardcoded 10000.0 m³/s placeholder
issues.body:
## Problem Statement

Two TODO comments in `src/sim/thermal_model_physics/physics_impl.rs` indicate that `ventilation_airflow` is hardcoded to a placeholder value instead of being read from the building specification:

```rust
// Line 927:
10000.0, // TODO: ventilation_airflow from building spec (m³/s)

// Line 3300:
10000.0, // TODO: ventilation_airflow from building spec (m³/s)
```

This means ventilation is not correctly coupling to the building specification. 10,000 m³/s is physically impossible (typical office is ~0.1–0.5 m³/s).

## Evidence

- Files: `src/sim/thermal_model_physics/physics_impl.rs` lines 927, 3300
- Hardcoded value: `10000.0` m³/s (placeholder — unrealistic)

## Impact

- Ventilation calculations use placeholder values instead of actual building specification
- Causes SOLAR-04 night ventilation failures
- Affects all ventilation-related validation

## Root Cause

The `from_spec` or building assembly parsing is not extracting the ventilation airflow rate and passing it to the physics implementation.

## Suggested Approach

1. **Trace the flow**: BuildingSpecification → ThermalModelData → physics_impl.rs
2. **Find where ventilation_airflow should come from**: Check `BuildingAssembly`, `ConstructionSet`, or zone specification
3. **Implement proper extraction**: Replace the TODO with actual value from building spec
4. **Add validation**: Ensure ventilation ACH matches ASHRAE 140 case definitions

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Both TODO lines replaced with actual `ventilation_airflow` from building spec
- [ ] Case 650 night ventilation shows different energy than Case 600 (night ventilation test)
- [ ] No regression in ventilation isolation tests

issues.title: feat(validation): Implement HVAC BESTEST RP-865 validation suite (#1754 follow-up)
issues.body:
## Problem Statement

Issue #1754 created the scaffolding for `tests/validation/hvac_bestest/` but the **actual BESTEST case definitions** (thermal capacity, COP curves, part-load ratios, furnace modules) were never implemented.

**Evidence**:
- Issue #1754: CLOSED — "Create `tests/validation/hvac_bestest/mod.rs` with module root" ✅
- Actual state: `tests/validation/hvac_bestest/` scaffold exists but no case definitions
- Reference: NREL TP-472-865 (HVAC BESTEST RP-865) defines test cases for System A (CAV), System B (VAV reheat), equipment

## Impact

- No way to validate HVAC equipment efficiency curves, part-load performance, or control strategies
- `release_gates.yaml` requires 60% pass rate but only ASHRAE 140 envelope cases are tested
- Blocks all HVAC optimization features (EMS, optimal start/stop, CO2-based DCV)

## Root Cause

1. HVAC case definitions require ASHRAE 90.1 efficiency curves and part-load ratio tables not yet in `fluxion_core::ashrae_cases`
2. The `HvacRunner` trait needs a `bestest_rp865_cases()` constructor
3. EnergyPlus `.idd` and `.epw` files for BESTEST weather year not in `tests/reference_data/`

## Suggested Approach

1. **Define case taxonomy** at `HvacBestestCase` enum: System A (CAV), System B (VAV reheat), Equipment cases
2. **Add ASHRAE 90.1 efficiency curves** to `ashrae_cases.rs`
3. **Implement HvacRunner::bestest_rp865_cases()** constructor
4. **Add 3-5 analytical BESTEST cases** (no reference data needed): E100 (CAV heating), E200 (CAV cooling), E300 (VAV reheat)

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `cargo test --test hvac_bestest` runs with at least 3 defined cases
- [ ] Each case has documented reference bounds and tolerance
- [ ] At least one case covers VAV terminal unit
- [ ] Integration test harness follows same pattern as `ashrae_140_case_600_series`

issues.title: feat(interop): Complete IDF → SimulationSchema conversion — HVAC, fenestration, schedules still missing
issues.body:
## Problem Statement

The basic `TryFrom<&IdfFile> for SimulationSchemaV1>` conversion landed in #1435, but design §10 of `docs/idf-import-design.md` explicitly marks three categories as **out of scope**:

1. **HVAC system objects** — `ZoneHVAC:*`, `Boiler:*`, `Chiller:*`, etc.
2. **FenestrationSurface:Detailed** — windows and doors
3. **Schedule objects** — `Schedule:Compact`, `ZoneControl:Thermostat`, etc.

The `case_spec_from_idf` workaround reads these directly from `IdfFile`, but this bypasses `SimulationSchemaV1` entirely.

## Evidence

- `src/io/idf/convert.rs:30-36`: Out-of-scope objects listed per design §10
- `docs/idf-import-design.md:275-295`: Three out-of-scope categories as follow-up issues
- `tests/idf_ashrae_140_acceptance.rs:280-281`: `case_spec_from_idf` reads setpoints/infiltration/windows directly — not via `SimulationSchemaV1`

## Impact

- Real EnergyPlus models with HVAC cannot be imported into Fluxion
- Fenestration cannot be modeled, breaking daylighting and solar gain accuracy
- Schedule-based controls are dropped, making dynamic simulations inaccurate

## Suggested Approach

1. **Fenestration**: Map `FenestrationSurface:Detailed` to `SimulationSchemaV1::Window`
2. **Schedules**: Map `Schedule:Compact` to `SimulationSchemaV1::Schedule`
3. **HVAC**: Map `ZoneHVAC:*` objects to `SimulationSchemaV1::HvacSystem`
4. **Add round-trip tests**: IDF → SimulationSchema → IDF preserves key fields

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `IdfFile` can be parsed from both IDF and epJSON formats
- [ ] `TryFrom<IdfFile> for SimulationSchemaV1` converts fenestration, schedules, HVAC
- [ ] Round-trip test preserves zone geometry and material layers
- [ ] At least one ASHRAE 140 case IDF with HVAC can be imported

issues.title: interop(ifc): IFC export is design-only — no round-trip tests, no lossless-field contract
issues.body:
## Problem Statement

`src/interop/ifc/writer.rs` produces syntactically-valid IFC4 STEP physical files but is "design-only (#1121)" — no guarantee that `SimulationSchemaV1` semantics survive the export.

**Evidence**:
- `src/interop/ifc/writer.rs` — writer module with `IfcBuilding`, `IfcSpace`, `IfcMaterialLayer`
- `ARCHITECTURE.md:985`: "IFC export still design-only (#1121)"
- No round-trip test exists (unlike OSM which has `test_roundtrip_single_zone`, `test_roundtrip_two_zones`)
- No lossless-field contract (OSM has explicit list in `src/interop/osm/mod.rs`)

## Impact

Users who want BIM → Fluxion → BIM workflows cannot verify model preservation through round-trip. Blocks adoption in BIM-centric workflows.

## Suggested Approach

1. **Define lossless-field contract**: Enumerate which `SimulationSchemaV1` fields IFC writer must preserve (zone geometry, material layer thicknesses, orientation, window-to-wall ratio)
2. **Add round-trip tests**: `import_ifc` → `export_ifc` → `import_ifc` with assertions on zone count, floor area, material layers
3. **Cover missing entities**: `IfcWindow`, `IfcDoor` entities not yet in writer

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Round-trip test: IFC → Fluxion → IFC preserves zone count, floor area, material layers
- [ ] `IfcWindow` and `IfcDoor` entities supported in writer
- [ ] Lossless-field contract documented in `src/interop/ifc/mod.rs`

issues.title: fix(interop): Case 600 IDF fixture wall R-value mismatch — 2.42 vs 1.79 m²K/W
issues.body:
## Problem Statement

The IDF fixture used for IDF-imported ASHRAE 140 validation has wall layers that produce a different R-value than the canonical ASHRAE 140 specification:

- **Fixture wall R-value**: `OUTR_WOOD` / `INSUL_R7` / `GYP_13` → **2.42 m²K/W**
- **ASHRAE 140 canonical wall R-value**: Plasterboard / Fiberglass / Wood Siding → **1.79 m²K/W**

This was documented in `tests/idf_ashrae_140_acceptance.rs:21-25`:

```rust
//! The Case 600 IDF fixture's wall layers yield R=2.42 m²K/W,
//! whereas ASHRAE 140 canonical Case 600 wall is 1.79 m²K/W.
```

## Evidence

- `tests/idf_ashrae_140_acceptance.rs:21-25` — explicit R-value mismatch documentation
- Fixture comment claims to match Case 600 but layer thicknesses differ

## Impact

- IDF-imported Case 600 simulation produces results for R=2.42, not R=1.79
- Comparing against EnergyPlus reference (generated with R=1.79) is apples-to-oranges
- `idf_ashrae_140_acceptance.rs` cannot actually validate the IDF import path

## Suggested Approach

1. **Fix the IDF fixture**: Update wall layer thicknesses to match ASHRAE 140 canonical values
2. **Re-validate**: Run IDF-imported Case 600 against E+ reference with corrected fixture
3. **Document**: Ensure fixture header accurately describes wall construction

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] IDF fixture wall R-value matches ASHRAE 140 canonical (1.79 m²K/W)
- [ ] IDF-imported Case 600 results within ±15% of E+ reference
- [ ] Fixture header comment accurately describes construction

issues.title: feat(performance): BatchOracle throughput — characterize actual vs 150 configs/sec CI gate
issues.body:
## Problem Statement

The `BatchOracle::evaluate_population` targets >10,000 configs/sec in documentation but the **release gate** requires only **150 configs/sec minimum**. No systematic characterization exists showing whether the engine reliably achieves the CI gate across:

- Physics-only (analytical) mode
- Surrogate mode (GPU ONNX inference)
- Multi-zone configurations (Case 960/970)
- Release vs debug builds

**Evidence**:
- `release_gates.yaml:72`: `min_configs_per_sec: 150` — hard CI gate
- `benches/batch_oracle_bench.rs:34`: "Target: >1000 configs/sec" — 6.7× the gate
- `tests/throughput_benchmark.rs:15`: `MINIMUM_THROUGHPUT = 100.0` — 2/3 of actual gate
- `tests/integration/test_batch_oracle.rs:79`: Only verifies ≥50 configs/sec — 1/3 of actual gate

## Impact

- `Fluxion Performance Gate (Issue #1618)` may pass or fail unpredictably if throughput hasn't been measured against the 150 configs/sec floor
- No visibility into throughput regression sources
- Multi-zone scaling bottleneck: `Case 960` has no throughput benchmark

## Root Cause Hypothesis

1. GPU batch construction overhead: `src/lib.rs:1262-1279` builds 24-hour cycle array per worker — O(n_zones × 8760) allocation
2. Multi-zone coupling overhead in `fluxion-core`
3. Rayon's `par_iter` fan-out not optimized for small populations

## Suggested Approach

1. **Add systematic throughput characterization test**: Vary config count (10-10,000), measure configs/sec
2. **Profile multi-zone overhead**: Isolate bottleneck in BatchOracle pipeline
3. **Set CI floor correctly**: Align test thresholds with actual release gate (150 configs/sec)

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Throughput characterization test covers 10-10,000 config range
- [ ] Multi-zone (Case 960) throughput benchmarked
- [ ] Test thresholds aligned with 150 configs/sec release gate
